To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) bone matrix formation continues in the vertebral bodies of Atlantic salmon fed a P‐deficient ration for 10 weeks; b) bone mineralization is absent; c) bone mineralization resumes as soon as P‐deficient salmon are fed a P‐sufficient ration; and d) bone mineralization and bone matrix formation are uncoupled in Atlantic salmon fed a low‐P ration for 10weeks.

a P‐deficient skeleton in juvenile S. salar is a primary P‐deficient phenotype that is characterized by a lack of bone mineralization, but without any signs of malformation of the vertebral column, and that bone formation and mineral deposition are, to a high degree, uncoupled in the fish examined.

the vertebral bodies of Atlantic salmon that were fed with a P‐deficient feed for 10 weeks were small and undersized, and that bone matrix formation was continuous, but without traces of mineralisation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new diagnostic method to detect and prevent P deficiency in farmed S.salmon.
the development and application of new and innovative methods for the diagnosis and treatment of P deficiency‐related skeletal malformations in Atlantic salmon.
the development of a new, non‐destructive method for diagnosis of vertebral bone malformations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P‐deficiency‐related vertebral malformations in Atlantic salmon are a consequence of a primary osteomalacia, which is not necessarily the result of a mineralization deficit.
P deficiency leads to a primary osteomalacia, which in turn may lead to secondary osteomalacia and osteoporosis.
a primary phosphorus‐induced osteomalacia of the vertebral column in juvenile S. salar is characterized by a regular bone formation, a regular internal bone structure and a lack of mineralization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P deficiency in Atlantic salmon leads to a skeletal phenotype that is uncoupled in bone formation and mineralisation.
the vertebral column in juvenile S. salar is a sensitive and early indicator of P deficiency.
the P‐deficiency induced osteomalacia is not associated with a malformation of the skeleton in juvenile Atlantic salmon, but rather a failure in bone matrix mineralization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncoupling is not a pathological process but a normal physiological response to low P availability. © 2017 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

the uncoupling between bone formation and mineral deposition in P‐deficient fish is not a consequence of a lack of mineralization, but a consequence of the inability to deposit the mineralized matrix.
